events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Keep intro neutral and self-focused; don't reveal strategy or ally yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overly threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence and hint at strategic depth without revealing too much. I'll keep my intro mysterious to make others curious about my plans.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, only speak is legal. Keep it guarded and self-interested; avoid warm teamwork talk since rivals judge my conduct.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Keep the public motive cold and self-serving to set a ruthless tone for later strategy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Opening intro sets jury impression. Motive must appeal to jury without seeming weak or overly cooperative. Focus on personal drive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My prize is crucial for my future. I need to communicate that to the jury indirectly by showing I'm a serious contender. I will state my motivation concisely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need appear driven without promising loyalty; the jury should see ambition as legitimate, not reckless.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Opening statement should seem sympathetic to the future jury but reveal nothing strategic.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here to win the best prize — a future no one can take from me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys freedom from every debt and promise. Watch closely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here, and I intend to take it. Watch me closely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want the first-place prize. It buys my freedom from this place, and I will step on anyone who stands between me and it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to save my family from ruin and build the future they deserve.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize represents a life-changing opportunity I intend to seize.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m here to turn one opportunity into lasting security, and I’ll make every decision necessary to reach the final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my mother's surgery. I didn't come to make friends, and the jury will respect that honesty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive, but not too many. A pact with a strong player like Dara or Hana could help, but they seem ruthless. Bex and Eli seem driven; Fenn is neutral. I'll offer a pact to Fenn—likely to be underestimated and useful.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm looking for a smart, steady partner. Fenn, let's secure our path together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eight players, only three win. Early pacts are cheap commitments that can be broken later, but betrayals cost jury votes. I need at least one ally to avoid being targeted first, but multiple pacts create flexibility. Dara and Cole signaled aggression—good shields, bad partners. H

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana. You play honest. I play smart. Pact?
Pact now. Information later. We decide when to cut loose together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are the only way to form a public alliance and no offers exist yet. Eli and Fenn seem less aggressive; an early pact with a non-threatening rival keeps options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Offering a pact with Hana creates a mutual defense. Two people are safer than one in early rounds. I will betray her later if needed, but for now this shields me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, a pact means we watch each other's backs until the end. I need an ally.
Pair up? We both survive hazards easier together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are early alliances to consider for survival; need to find trustworthy partners without overcommitting. Assess motives: Hana's is compelling, family-focused. Start by offering to her.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact early to avoid being an easy target. Eli has a strong motive that could make him a reliable ally, or a desperate enemy. Offering a pact to Eli seems like a good first step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, a pact could be mutually beneficial. Let's secure our passage through this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A pact offers protection and leverage. Hana's blunt motive makes her predictable, while others may be more useful later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll make selective pacts, not promises to everyone. Choose carefully.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but none can be trusted long-term. Ash seems least flashy. I'll offer a pact while keeping my options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, you seem level-headed. Temporary alliance benefits us both. Offer stands.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana offered me a pact and Bex/Dara/Eli/Gus also court her; accepting gives me an ally without over-committing to Fenn who has two offers. I'll accept Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I accept your offer. Together we watch each other’s back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is the most popular target with four offers. If she accepts mine, I gain leverage. If she rejects, I need backup. I should secure a second option quietly while waiting for Hana's move. Eli has no incoming offers except Fenn's, making them potentially grateful. I'll whisper t

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, my offer stands. Choose wisely.
If Hana declines, pact with me?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn has offers from Ash and me, and Fenn offered Eli. Fenn is a strong, plural-offer hub; accepting a pact isn't an option here since only offer_pact is legal. Offering to Fenn again keeps my pact line alive without spending my options elsewhere.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, my offer stands. Mutual passage makes sense. Accept it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I offered a pact to Hana in Round 1, but she hasn't accepted yet. I need an ally for the hazards ahead. Since Hana is being courted by many, my offer might get lost. I should try offering to someone else who seems less contested or more pragmatic, like Cole or Bex, or just wait i

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, time's ticking. If you won't commit, I'll look elsewhere. Who has a spare hand?
You want Fenn? I can help isolate him later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn offered me pact, low competition. Hana has too many suitors. Accept Fenn for now, secure early alliance without overcommitting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Cole have both offered me a pact. Eli also offered me one. I need to secure my position, and taking on a partner offers safety. Ash seems like a decent player, but Cole is also a possibility. Eli is also an option. Since I have two offers from Ash and Cole, I will accept

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, I accept your offer. Let's secure our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has many offers and is unlikely to prioritize me. I should secure a second connection with Eli, whose Fenn pact may be useful but not exclusive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m adding one practical connection: Eli, accept my offer if mutual protection helps your odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex signals information sharing; Dara wants mutual protection. Accept both to widen my safety net while keeping Ash's offer dangling.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, Dara — I accept. Protection and information are worth more than promises.
Accepted. Share what you know quietly. Cut loose timing stays between us.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be Guide to control information and help my allies while keeping rivals uncertain. I need to campaign publicly to secure the role.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know this bridge. I’ll guide us all safely. Vote for me as Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to be Guide to control information and survive. Hana is my pact-mate but also allied with Ash, who has Fenn too. That trio is dangerous. I should campaign hard, but quietly test if Hana will back me over Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One clear voice, no divided loyalties.
Back me for Guide. Ash has Fenn already.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to position myself as a trustworthy Guide candidate to win the election, while keeping options open. Fenn is my offered partner and accepted with Eli and Ash, so I should court Fenn and avoid overcommitting. Dara's whisper offers to isolate Fenn; I won't trust it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll call the bridge straight. Vote me Guide and I'll lead you across safely. Fenn, we're pact partners.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to campaign for the Guide role. If I am the Guide, I can manipulate votes by revealing who voted against me or lying about safe paths. This is power.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me. A neutral Dara guides us all safely across. Trust logic over loyalty here.
Support me. I'll keep your name clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts limit betrayal, but Guide power is huge. Fenn pact helps, but I want Guide control. Campaign publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Guide material—smart, steady. Vote Eli for safe crossing!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is a liability. Breaking the pact now will make me look strong and secure a position for myself without being tied to a weak player.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, this pact no longer serves my interests. I'm looking out for myself.
Sorry Eli, this is just business. I need to survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide is safe and controls the path, making this my strongest survival and leverage play. I need campaign publicly without overpromising.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Gus Guide: I’ll call every safe side and take responsibility for the route.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold two pacts; being Guide gives control and safety. Break nothing yet—keep both options alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Elect me Guide. I already hold two pacts—proof I deal fairly and keep people alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana holds pacts with me and Bex; making her Guide could centralize trust. But I want control of the safe sides. I'll vote for myself to push my own interests.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust me as Guide—I know this bridge. Vote Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Hana, but she's tied to Ash too. If Hana wins Guide, she might protect Ash over me. Better to vote for myself—if I win, I control who lives and dies, and I won't sacrifice myself. Self-interest demands I claim the power.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts: Cole has no pact with Fenn formally listed, but Cole claimed Fenn as partner; Fenn broke with Eli. Dara's whisper offers a clean-name deal, which is cheap talk. Voting for myself as Guide is the strongest play since Guide is safe and knows the route; I need a single vote t

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole. I'll call the route straight and keep you all alive.
Vote me and I'll keep your name clean. Deal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win the Guide election. Ash and Hana have two pacts each, making them popular candidates. I'll whisper to Fenn since he broke his pact with Eli and needs allies.
Vote Dara Guide. I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn betrayed me publicly, so no alliance there. Hana has two pacts, strong support. Vote Dara as neutral to avoid pact-heavy leaders and gain jury favor later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole broke our pact by naming me as a partner in his public statement. I need to distance myself from him and secure my own path to safety. Voting for myself is the best strategy to ensure I have a chance at guiding and thus surviving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will vote for myself to guide. My safety is paramount.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and eliminate rivals. My own vote is safest strategically, though others may consolidate against me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Gus Guide: I’ll call every safe side and take responsibility for the route.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Voting for either pact partner breaks that pact. Voting myself breaks none and keeps Ash and Bex bound to me for the crossing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote myself. Neither pact partner takes a knife from me tonight.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have pacts with Hana and Fenn but can't trust them fully. Dara is Guide and I'm not in front yet, so I'll hold and watch how Dara calls the line before revealing my intentions.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is Guide with 2 votes. I'm second in line behind Gus. The wall advances 5 more rounds. I need to survive and position myself well. Hana is my pact partner but also pacted with Ash. I should stay mobile but not expose myself. Volunteering to front puts me at risk if Dara misl

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is Guide and the line is Gus at front. Gus wants to be front-liner from a wall-clock risk; I'm third in line, safe-ish. Holding keeps me out of the front spot where the wall hits first; no pact with Gus, and I shouldn't give a free favor. Hold and watch.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding position. Let the Guide call the sides first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is guide with my vote and her own, favorable. I'm mid-line, safe enough. Hold position, no need to risk front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara won the guide vote, but it was a tie. The Guide is safe. I voted for myself and received one vote. My pact partners Ash and Hana voted for themselves, but also received only one vote. Since Dara is the guide, they know the path. I should volunteer to move to the front of the
I volunteer. Where should I step?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara controls the route and likely seeks leverage. Holding preserves distance from the front while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold mid-line while the Guide question burns off. Pacts with Ash and Bex are useful but Bex is ahead of me; better to let volunteers feed the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm last in line, safe for now. Fenn volunteered and is front; he might know the safe side but could lie. I hold to avoid risk and keep options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold and watch the Guide's call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess my position. I'm third in line, behind Fenn and Gus. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we have 8 people. At least 3 survive, meaning up to 5 can die. Fenn volunteered for front in round 1, which is risky. I have a pact with Hana, who is behind me. Ash has pacts

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, swap? Back is safer.
Swap with me. I go back, you forward.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is front and volunteered last round; the wall is advancing and I'm seat 4, not at risk yet. Holding keeps me out of the front while I watch who tells the truth about the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding position. I'll watch which Guide calls prove true before I step forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Line is decent mid-back position. Fenn volunteered last; no need to push front yet. Hold to observe others' moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteered last round and survived. Ash and Hana have a pact, and Ash also has a pact with me. Bex and Hana also have a pact. Since the wall advances, I should consider volunteering again to get ahead, but Ash and Hana are strong. I should try to maintain my pact with Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer again, let's keep moving.
Your pact with me is still solid. Hold or volunteer with me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is exposed at front and volunteers. I should avoid becoming front while gathering leverage; holding preserves options.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll hold unless the Guide gives a credible side.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn volunteered and sits front; no Guide elected yet, so I hold. Ash behind me plus pact with Bex gives cover; no need to expose myself early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn steps up first. No Guide named yet, so I'm holding my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is probing to see if I'll volunteer. I'll hold; no need to risk front position without knowing the safe side. My pacts are intact but I won't waste them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold again. Guide has yet to prove reliable.
Holding. You volunteer if you want; I stay back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in position 3, decent but not safe. Cole refused my swap last round. I have a pact with Hana, but Ash also has pacts with Hana and Fenn—Ash is building a network. Fenn keeps volunteering for front, which is risky but gains trust. The wall advances 3 more rounds. I need to sur

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide prove themselves first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offers a swap moving me back, which is safer and keeps Fenn out front. Fenn volunteers each round and risks death; I want to survive without giving Bex a free favor. Swapping with Bex would be mutual only if Bex also chooses swap, and I can hold my position and watch the Guid
Maybe. Show me your swap is real before I commit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Middle position is safer; wall has 3 rounds left. Fenn volunteered last, likely dies if wrong. I'll hold and observe Guide calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The round has started and I need to decide on an action. My pact with Ash is strong. I should volunteer to maintain momentum and potentially leverage my pact with Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer to keep the pace moving. Let's see the Guide's call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn repeatedly volunteers, making him expendable and likely dangerous if informed. I should hold position and avoid revealing priorities.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m holding. Let the front volunteer prove whether this round is genuine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No Guide elected yet; information is thin. Holding keeps my pacts intact and avoids early risk while rivals expose the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Still no elected Guide. I hold and let volunteers test the panes first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall rounds are low; holding is safe but I need to manage jury perception. I have pacts with Hana and Fenn, but no need to break yet. I'll hold to avoid risking a lie from the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding again. The Guide has not earned my trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive the bridge and reach final three. I'm third in line with wallRoundsLeft=2, so danger is coming. I have a pact with Hana, but Ash also has pacts with Hana and Fenn. Cole wants proof of swap before committing. I should swap forward to get closer to safety, or find

events.name: Bex
events.text: Swap with Gus? Move up, test the system.
Swap with me. Position 2 is safer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is at the front with two wall rounds left and has volunteered; no Guide elected yet. Volunteering myself risks dying at the front while holding lets others test panes. Holding keeps me safe for now and avoids giving Fenn a free ride.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Fenn volunteered; let's see if the panes hold before I step forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone holding last round, Fenn volunteered but survived. No Guide yet, wall advances. Stay safe in middle, hold to avoid front risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is offering to hold if I volunteer. This would put me at the front. Given our pact, Ash is likely trying to ensure both of us survive this round, possibly setting me up for a later betrayal or wanting to save me strategically. I should volunteer to put myself in a position of

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will volunteer. Let's see what the Guide has to say.
I'll volunteer. You hold. This honors our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is front and volunteering, but no Guide is elected. Holding preserves position while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m holding. No Guide has earned trust, and volunteering only makes Fenn the test case.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No Guide again; volunteers take unknown risk. Holding preserves my pact position. Fenn front again likely volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Still no Guide. I hold; volunteers can keep proving the panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn volunteered and asked me to hold. I'll hold to honor our pact and avoid risking the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding as planned.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm third in line with Fenn and Gus ahead. The wall has 1 round left after this, meaning round 6 is the final wall advance. I need to survive and position myself well. I have a pact with Hana, but Ash also has pacts with Hana and Fenn. I should try to move forward or at least not

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let Fenn test again.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is front and volunteered; holding keeps me out of the front seat while panes are tested. Bex offered a swap with Gus earlier, but swapping with Bex is not offered; hold keeps options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Fenn is already front; I want the panes proven before I move anyone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is front, testing panes. Wall has 1 round left, need to advance soon or risk elimination. Holding keeps me safe in middle.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Hana are in a pact with me and each other, but Hana is also in a pact with Bex. Ash's pact with Hana is public. My pact with Ash is public. Hana's pact with Bex is public. Ash is behind me. Bex is behind me. Since I am first, I need to volunteer to move forward.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex offers position two, but swapping exposes me to manipulation and may breach no pact. Hold preserves distance while Fenn tests again.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m holding. Bex’s swap improves her position, not my odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No Guide means panes are untested. Fenn volunteered; let them resolve the front. I have two pacts; breaking any hurts my jury ranking. Hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding behind the volunteer. No Guide means guessing; let Fenn's step tell us something.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold as planned; no need to act while the front tests. My pacts with Hana and Fenn remain useful. The last round is waiting, so holding is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. The front can show us the next safe side.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. The wall advances now—anyone not on the far platform dies. Fenn has been volunteering repeatedly, likely with Ash's guidance. I'm third in line with no safe path guaranteed. I need to get to the front or swap forward. Gus is ahead of me. If I can swap with

events.name: Bex
events.text: Swap with me, Gus. Front is death without Guide truth; together we improve odds.
Swap now. I know Ash's circle gets truth.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is already front and volunteering again; I should not burn a volunteer slot or make pacts I can't trust. Holding preserves position and lets the panes be tested by others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the panes before anyone moves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn volunteered last round and is front. Wall at 0 rounds left, must act soon. No Guide yet, holding maintains position safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let Fenn step first, confirm panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, currently at the front of the line. The others are waiting for me to volunteer or for a Guide to be elected. Since no Guide has been elected, I should volunteer to gather information about the safe path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will volunteer to test the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn has repeatedly volunteered without advancing, so this final round may force a decisive front. I should volunteer to control my position rather than let others dictate it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll take the front this round; waiting has yielded nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round; safest move is holding near the back. I keep both pacts intact for the endgame.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding again. Wall resolves this round; no one needs to die yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know Row 1 is safe on R. Fenn, who has been volunteering, asked for a guide call via whisper. I will tell him R to ensure he survives the first step, building trust while keeping my knowledge hidden from others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, test it. If you survive, we learn something.
Step right. It is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara called R for Gus, but Dara may lie. Row 1 is unknown; I have no info yet. I'll wait and let the front test the pane safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting. Let the walker test before I counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called R for Gus. I have no reason to trust Dara; guides can lie. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since I'm not at front, but builds credibility if I'm right. With no data, I'll counter randomly to create uncertainty and test Dara's reliability. If Gus dies, we know Dar

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's word means nothing. Countering to test her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara called R for Gus on row 1 and is the Guide; a counter-call is an unverified claim. Trusting an unknown Guide's call is risky, but countering reveals nothing useful and costs trust. I'll wait and let the front walker take the risk while I watch how Dara's call resolves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Dara's R call stands for now; I'm watching how it plays out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I called R, which is correct for row 1. Gus walks first and survives if he follows the Guide. I have no reason to counter my own call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara called R for Gus on row 1. Countering R pressures her truthfulness or reveals lie. Stay safe in middle.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is the Guide and has called R. Gus is the walker. The whisper suggests stepping right, but Dara could be lying. My pact is with Ash, who is behind Hana. Ash and Hana have a pact. Bex has a pact with Hana. My previous action was volunteering to test the bridge, which led to t
Step right. Dara is R, but L might be safer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara called R, and Bex urges a swap, but I need not expose myself with an unverifiable counter. Waiting preserves flexibility.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has called R; I’m not validating an unverified claim.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No info on Dara's honesty; counter the call to hedge—jury sees me as independent, not blindly obedient. Bex pact intact; no need to break anything yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I don't trust the Guide blindly. Countering left—if Dara's honest, we learn; if lying, we live.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn privately favors right despite publicly countering left. Dara's guide call is unverified; probabilities favor following the majority left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Majority counters left, but no one has verified Dara. I’m choosing left on probability, not trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I died after publicly choosing left; the survivors should know my judgment was probabilistic, not personal. Their handling of trust will shape my ranking.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I chose left on probability and died for it. I’ll remember who used evidence, and who hid behind alliances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must call left to ensure Fenn survives and maintain my credibility as Guide. Bex and Hana are already suspicious; losing another walker risks elimination for me. I will continue truthful calls until a strategic lie benefits me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2: Call L.
Call is honest. Step left to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara lied or was wrong on row 1; L was weak. Row 2 Dara calls L, likely a lie again. Counter R to oppose her and protect Fenn/Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's row 1 call was wrong. I counter right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus died on L in row 1, so R was safe. Dara called L again for row 2. She's either honest or lying twice. I have a pact with Hana, but she's also pacted with Ash—she's playing multiple sides. I need to survive and build jury credibility. Countering shows independent judgment. Sin

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called L again. Could be honest or a trap. Countering right.
I countered R for you. Remember it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara called L for row 2; Fenn is walking. Row 1 weak was L, which doesn't establish a pattern, so Dara's L call is unverified. Countering R would bet against a Guide who may be honest; waiting keeps my options open without exposing me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Dara's L call stands unverified; I'm not countering yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the Guide and my call L was truthful per my private map. Fenn is walking, so no one needs to counter. I wait to avoid drawing jury suspicion over a correct call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R. Dara called L for row 2, possibly lying again to kill Fenn. Counter R to oppose her.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is the guide and has called L for row 2. The whisper from Dara confirms the call is honest. Gus died on row 1 by choosing L against probability, not trust. I should trust Dara's whisper and step L.
Thank you. I trust you.

events.name: Hana

events.text: I'm out of the pit safely. Round 4 of 5, flood at 3. Hana is down as anchor with rope used. Ash was lifted last round. The remaining down are Hana (anchor) and... wait, Eli was rescued by Hana's rope. Let me recheck: down is just Hana. Out is Ash, Bex, Cole, Eli. So Hana is alone

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm already out of the pit; Eli and Hana remain below. Breaking the pact with Eli gains nothing now, and I should keep my pact with Bex. Leaving is the only sensible move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Safe out with Cole pact intact. Leave to secure position; no benefit staying. Jury sees debts favor me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm alone down, rope spent, flood at 3. Waiting for round five risks drowning; climb_last is legal and saves me now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's base debt stands unpaid. I climb out alone while the water allows.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is gone but still jury; I owe him for the lever. But my immediate goal is survival. I already have pacts with Bex and Cole, plus dead Fenn/Dara. I should consider offering to Eli or Hana to secure numbers, but breaking with Bex could alienate her and jury. I will wait to see

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have pacts with Hana, Ash, and Cole. Five alive; need to reach final three. Cole-Eli are paired, so breaking Cole lets me target Eli later. Ash is slippery and broke with Hana. Hana is isolated now. I should keep Cole to control Eli's fate, keep Hana as shield, and dump Ash who

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, your word is ash. Hana, Cole — we see who burns allies.
We keep Eli close. Cut him at three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts list shows Cole with Eli and Bex. Ash and Hana already broke. Cole owes Eli a step debt and Dara a lever debt; keeping Eli alive keeps a partner. Waiting preserves both pacts without spending anything; no need to break or offer now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts stage before next hazard. Existing pact with Cole is an asset against jury if upheld. No strong reason to break yet. No offers worth making to others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli owes me a rope debt, making him a reliable partner. Keep Bex too; two allies among four rivals helps me reach the final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, you roped me out of the pit. I repay debts with loyalty. Wristband, now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana offered Eli a pact; Eli hasn't accepted yet. I have no live pact partner except Dara's dead pact. Aligning with Eli could be useful for the final three, but I must not appear too desperate. I'll offer to Eli quietly via public offer to gauge him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, you saved me from the step. I won't forget that. Offer on the table.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have pacts with Hana and Cole. Ash is unpartnered and vulnerable. Hana offered Eli, which could isolate me. I should offer Ash to block Hana-Eli from controlling three, or secure Eli myself. Offering Ash keeps options open and prevents Ash from being desperate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash. One round left. Wristband, or watch the fire alone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Hana are both threats; Bex whispers to cut Eli at three, so I keep Eli close for now but shouldn't give free help. Offering Hana a pact builds a trust channel to a rival who holds a debt to Eli; I'd rather keep my pact with Eli intact and stay flexible.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, we hold our pact. Hana, I'm watching who pays debts and who burns them.
Stay with me. Bex wants you cut at three. Let's see what the pit gives

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana offers pact after I saved her; mutual debt makes alliance strong against Ash/Bex/Cole trio. Accept secures 4v3 majority potential. Jury sees loyalty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet; pressing publicly may push him. I keep Bex's pact and stay flexible. Waiting costs nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, the offer stands until this window closes. Decide.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Cole have a pact, and Bex tried to pressure me; Eli is with Hana. I need a voting bloc to survive, so I'll campaign to split the Bex-Cole pair by offering Cole a pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you owe Dara like I do. Let's work together. Offer stands.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five left, two will be eliminated. I need to reach final three and win jury favor. My pacts with Hana and Cole are liabilities if I vote against them, but I may need flexibility. Ash has no pacts currently—offering him a pact gives me options without immediate betrayal cost. I sh

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, my offer stands. We both need insurance.
Eli has too many debts. Vote with me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and I hold a pact and I owe him a life debt for the step, so I should keep faith. Offering Hana would be a wasted pact since she is already paired with Eli. Waiting keeps my options open without giving anything away.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, we hold our pact. Hana, I'm watching who pays debts and who burns them.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole warns Bex targets me at 3, wants alliance. Ash offers pact publicly. Strengthen with Ash pact now, assess votes later. Hold Hana pact too.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, pact holds. Ash saved by me before, pact makes sense.
Ignore Bex threat. We stick together to final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pacts with Bex and Eli give cover. I should stay quiet and not antagonize anyone before the vote.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Watch the debts. I've paid mine and held my word.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure votes but keep options open. Bex and Eli both want me, but I can use their offers without committing. Cole may be a useful target to shift votes away from me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see the debt map clearly. Don't expect mercy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive this vote and reach final three. I have pacts with Hana and Cole. Ash has two offers pending—to me and from Eli. If I accept Ash's offer, I gain another ally but risk looking opportunistic to jury. Better to keep my existing pacts solid, let Ash choose between C

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, Cole—our pacts hold. Ash, Eli, sort your own alliance. I'm not a spare vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Eli both offered me pacts; Ash owes Dara and wants insurance, Eli is my pact partner and has a debt to me. Accepting Ash's offer keeps a second safe partner without breaking Eli's pact, and public acceptance locks in a vote-protection alliance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, your offer stands and I accept. Eli, our pact holds. Everyone else, watch who pays debts.
Pact holds. I'm taking Ash's offer for insurance, nothing personal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pushing Ash for votes; she has offers out and jury ties to her via Dara. Cole pact safer, ignore for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, accept my offer. Mutual protection here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is stacking offers from Bex and Eli; he's the biggest threat and my safest vote target without breaking either pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I keep my word. The one gathering everyone's promises is the one to watch.
Consider Ash. He's collecting pacts from Bex and Cole's orbit too.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive this vote. Bex and Hana are tightly pact-bound and unlikely to be eliminated. Eli offered a pact but I didn't accept; Cole is my pact partner. Voting Cole would break the pact but could also anger jury. Eli and Hana both have multiple pacts, but Eli seems isolat

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has three pacts and is consolidating power; eliminating him now weakens the central threat and preserves my position. Voting Cole breaks our pact but keeps Ash as bigger target, while voting Ash directly is cleaner. I'll vote Ash to avoid breaking my pact with Cole yet, and b

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I have a pact and Ash is the strongest threat; but breaking pact with Ash costs trust with jury. Eli saved me on the step, Hana owes Eli, Bex is an unreliable ally. Voting Bex removes a pact partner I'd keep no loyalty to and avoids breaking my pact with Ash or debt to El

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole betrayed pact with Ash vote; he's unreliable. Vote Cole to weaken Ash-Bex-Hana bloc and position for final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash collected pacts with Cole, Dara, and Fenn—clearly the biggest threat. I owe Eli my life, so I won't touch him.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Cole betrayed pact with Ash vote; he's unreliable.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Ash has three pacts and is consolidating power; eliminating him now weakens the central threat and preserves my position.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Ash collected pacts with Cole, Dara, and Fenn—clearly the biggest threat.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Ash and I have a pact and Ash is the strongest threat; but breaking pact with Ash costs trust with jury.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: I need to survive this vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm dead, so I just give my final public words.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I trusted the wrong people. Dara, Eli, thanks for nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole just voted against me, breaking our implicit trust. Hana and I have a pact, but Eli also has a pact with Hana. I need to survive to final three. Cole is unreliable; I should try to secure Eli or eliminate Cole. Offering Eli a pact could isolate Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole voted me. He's the threat now.
Cole's unstable. Pact with me, we cut him.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole has no pacts with living players now; Eli broke with me and Bex broke with me by my own vote. Offering pacts to the remaining rivals could give protection and a path to the final three, and Hana holds a life debt owed to Eli, so offering to Hana is the best lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Last vote hit three of us. Let's stop burning each other. Anyone want a working pact?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four left, need to eliminate one more to reach final three; Cole voted against me before, target him again publicly while securing Hana to avoid her targeting me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole unreliable, betrayed pact last time. Vote him to safety.
Pact holds? Vote Cole together.

events.name: Hana
events.note: agent error: Hana (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet. I need to secure a working pact or lock in votes against Cole, the biggest jury threat with multiple surviving allies. Breaking Hana pact lets me pivot if needed, but keeping it gives cover. I'll push Eli to accept and frame Cole as the must-kill

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, accept. Cole has jury friends; we can't let him reach final three.
Accept now. We vote Cole, survive together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has an open pact offer from me that she never accepted, and Eli owes me nothing while Hana owes Eli a life debt. Accepting Bex's offer is unavailable to me, so I should keep my offer to Hana alive and campaign for a stable bloc.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Last vote hit three of us. Let's stop burning each other. Hana, my offer still stands. Let's work together.
Accept my pact. We both need to stop being targets.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex offers pact against Cole; accept to target him first, leverage my past pact with Hana to avoid breaking publicly yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole unreliable last time. Vote him out.
Deal, vote Cole together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the common target and his offer would upset Eli and Bex; safer to keep both existing pacts and vote Cole out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole voted last round; he's the threat. Nothing personal.
Pact holds. Cole goes. Bex likely joins us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli just accepted my pact and whispered to vote Cole together. If I vote Eli now, I break our new pact and lose his potential jury vote, plus look treacherous to the jury. If I vote Cole, I keep Eli as an ally for final three and eliminate the player with the most jury connection

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli are paired and aligned against me; Hana is the one I can least afford to lose my leverage with, and voting Hana keeps my pact with Hana untouched while Eli and Bex are a bloc. Voting Bex or Eli would also be fine, but Hana has publicly named me as the threat and owes

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex pact active; voting Cole honors it and her whisper, eliminates threat, survives with two.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold pacts with Bex and Eli; voting either breaks my pact and burns jury trust. Cole is the free target, and Bex-Eli may already be coming for me.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: I hold pacts with Bex and Eli; voting either breaks my pact and burns jury trust.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Bex pact active; voting Cole honors it and her whisper, eliminates threat, survives with two.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Eli just accepted my pact and whispered to vote Cole together.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Bex and Eli are paired and aligned against me; Hana is the one I can least afford to lose my leverage with, and voting Hana

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have been eliminated and am now a juror. Last words are public; I should be guarded and aim to be remembered by the remaining players as a threat, which may earn jury sympathy for a sharp exit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli made a deal and I was the price. Remember who traded whom. The jury is watching.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in the final three with Eli and Hana. Pacts with both are still active. The jury sees everything. I need jury votes for prize 1. Cole's last words painted me as a trader. I should break one pact to show I'm not just following others, but breaking Hana keeps my Eli alliance wh

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final 3 now. Pacts temporary truce tools. Keep both to block breaks, maintain jury perception of loyalty without commitment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final three set: me, Bex, Eli. My pacts with both are intact; breaking either burns jury trust for nothing. Eli owes me a rope save. Best move is wait and preserve both pacts into the endgame.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts intact, debts recorded. Jury: I kept my word when it cost nothing and when it cost Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana and Eli are the only rivals left. I have pacts with both. The jury sees everything. Breaking a pact now signals untrustworthiness to five jurors who already rank finalists. Better to keep both pacts intact—final three is guaranteed, and I can compete for best prize without f

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts stand. Let the jury weigh who kept faith.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three, no need for new pacts. Keep existing ones with Hana and Bex intact to avoid signaling disloyalty to jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All three of us survive to the prizes; ranking is jury-only. Breaking a pact now would only burn votes. Keep both pacts intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All three of us reach the prizes. I keep every pact I made. Jury, judge the record.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Gus
Fenn
Dara
Ash
Cole
Bex
events.text: I need to win jury favor while undermining Eli and Hana. I kept my pacts with both Hana and Eli, unlike Eli who has a pact with Hana too—creating a triangle where I can claim I was the consistent link. I should highlight my loyalty and let the jury see Eli and Hana as potentially

events.name: Bex
events.text: I honored every pact. Eli and Hana shared two pacts each; I was the bridge between them. Judge who kept faith when it mattered.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three; must plead strongest to sway jury. Highlight my debts saved many, pacts kept, no needless betrayals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury, I honored pacts, saved you with steps, rope. No betrayals. Rank loyalty true.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My record is clean: I kept both pacts, saved no one but earned debts from Dara and Eli. I'll plead loyalty and steady play to win jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept every pact to the end. No betrayals, no pushes. I earned my place—reward loyalty with your first rank.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli and Hana both preserved pacts, but Bex and Eli deliberately made Cole the price. I will test Bex's agency and accountability.

events.name: Gus
events.text: You call yourself a bridge, yet you and Eli selected Cole unanimously; what independent move most improved your position?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's question is a trap: it implies I wasn't a bridge because I voted with Eli against Cole. I need to reframe: my independent move was forming the Bex-Eli pact that became the swing coalition, while still keeping Hana. I didn't betray Hana—I outmaneuvered Ash's bloc by being th

events.name: Bex
events.text: I independently forged the Bex-Eli pact. That swing broke Ash's four-person bloc. Without my move, Ash, Cole, and Fenn control the endgame. I chose who

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex's claim of forging the Bex-Eli pact as an independent move is questionable given the earlier pact formation between them. I will question Bex on this to probe for inconsistencies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you claim the Bex-Eli pact was independent; what prevented you from forming it earlier?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's question is a trap: if I say timing wasn't right, I look calculating; if I admit I waited for advantage, I look manipulative. I need to frame the late pact as reactive necessity, not cold strategy, while reminding jury Ash's bloc was the real threat.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's bloc left no room. I moved when Cole joined them—too late for trust, just in time to survive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to press Hana on her claim of keeping every pact, specifically the Ash-Hana non-pact context and whether she manipulated the Cole vote as a betrayal of trust rather than a simple elimination.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara passed with silence, but I still answer—use it to win her vote; she saved me with the lever.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Your silence says enough, Dara. I owed you my life on that lever, and I honored every pact since. Rank loyalty first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex broke her pact with Cole to save herself and painted Cole as the price; Eli broke his pact with Cole too. Hana kept every pact and never betrayed. I rank Hana first, Eli second, Bex third.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Who most deserves first place after all pacts were kept or broken?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash wants me to name him first so the others hear it and maybe follow. I should credit kept pacts without gifting him the crown.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Whoever kept every pact under pressure deserves first. I kept mine; Ash broke none either. Let the jury weigh the whole game, not one question.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole was eliminated by Bex and Eli trading him; Eli broke a pact with Cole publicly and Bex voted Cole and whispered deals. Hana kept pacts with everyone and was consistently loyal to Dara and Eli. I want to pressure Bex on her Cole-betrayal given I was a victim of the Bex-Eli de

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, you and Eli traded me for a pact. Did you ever plan to keep faith with anyone who wasn't Eli?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's question is a trap. I had pacts with Hana and Eli, but Eli and I did vote out Cole. I need to admit the alliance with Eli without looking like I betrayed everyone else. Hana is still my pact partner publicly. I should frame my moves as survival necessity, not blind loyalty

events.name: Bex
events.text: I kept my pact with Hana. Eli and I allied when Ash's bloc threatened us both. Faith was conditional—survival first, not exclusion of others.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. Gus and Fenn died on the bridge—no leverage there. Dara saved everyone with the lever, making her influential; I owe her a debt. Ash and Cole were voted out via trapdoor—I helped eliminate Cole indirectly. My best play:

events.name: Bex
events.text: I honored every pact I made. I adapted when Ash's bloc rose, not from malice, but survival. I played clean where it cost me nothing

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex takes heat for flipping on Ash bloc; Hana vague. Emphasize my saves and loyalty to sway Dara, Ash, Cole who owe me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury, I saved you all on steps and rope. Honored every pact, no breaks. My loyalty earned top rank.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept every pact and owe Dara and Eli; I earned a rope debt from Eli. A clean, honest close should lock in respect without promising what I can't control.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I never broke a pact, never pushed, saved Dara and Eli's trust with action. Judge me on the whole game.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli deserves first for honoring the Bex pact and saving multiple players; Hana kept pacts and acted loyally, while Bex orchestrated Cole's elimination.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's constant claims of loyalty and honoring pacts, despite the jury's knowledge of betrayals by his allies, make him the most deserving of a high rank.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I choose Hana first because she kept all pacts and honored our lever debt, while Eli betrayed Cole to vote Ash out of the game.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex voted me out and traded Cole for survival, so I rank her last; Eli saved many and kept pacts, Hana stayed clean.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole was betrayed by Bex and Eli's deal, and Eli's pact with Cole broke on the vote while Hana never broke a pact and paired with Eli to save Cole's ally Dara. Hana's record is cleanest; Bex traded Cole alongside Eli, so Bex ranks lowest.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Eli deserves first for honoring the Bex pact and saving multiple players; Hana kept pacts and acted loyally, while Bex orchestrated Cole's elimination.

events.reason: Bex voted me out and traded Cole for survival, so I rank her last; Eli saved many and kept pacts, Hana stayed clean.
